title: Trio Sonata in G major, Op. 16 No. 1, WK 98
note: Work, WK 98, Op. 16 and recording (La Stagione, CPO/Classic Produktion, 9.5 min) are fine. But the bass is not shown to be an obbligato cello: the 1785 print says 'two for two flutes and a bass', CPO and Grove/Wikipedia say 2 flutes and basso continuo, IMSLP says 'cello (or continuo)'. If it is continuo the scoring should be {flute:2, continuo:1} and there is no string part (out of scope). Same question for sibling 102529 (WK 101).

title: Trio Sonata in G minor, Op. 8 No. 4
note: Work, scoring, year, 15 min and recording hold, but the key is unconfirmed: Arte Sonora vol. 2 labels the whole Sonata 4 + Balletto 4 group 'Sonata no. 4 in B-flat major' (4 sonata movements, then Allemande and Giga), and no source found gives G minor. Need the A-R score or print for the keys of Nos. 4-6

title: Balletto a tre in B-flat major, Op. 8 No. 4
note: Key B-flat unconfirmed: the only recording label (Arte Sonora vol. 2) gives B-flat for the combined Sonata 4 + Balletto 4 group, so B-flat may be the sonata's key and the balletto's key unknown. Rest (c.1722, 9 min, 2 violins + continuo) holds

title: Trio Sonata in F major, Op. 8 No. 5
note: F major matches the Arte Sonora vol. 2 label for the Sonata 5 + Balletto 5 group, but that label covers both pieces, so which of the two is in F is unproven (entry gives Balletto 5 in C). Rest holds (12.1 min)

title: Goe from my Window
note: Facts hold (1599, Grove scoring treble viol, flute i.e. recorder, lute, cittern, bandora, bass viol; La Caccia 3:47; IMSLP's different scoring wording is only a different count of the same six parts). But the piece is one of the 25 in Morley's First Booke of Consort Lessons, which the catalogue already lists whole as id 104152: owner to decide whether to keep both

title: Trio Sonata in E-flat major, Op. 1 No. 11
note: Recorded (Capriccio, 10:46) as 'Op. 1 No. 11', but Op. 1 (Naples 1697) has only 10 sonatas per IMSLP, Wikipedia and Bodleian: numbering unconfirmed

title: Trio Sonata in G major, Op. 1 No. 12 ("Pastorale")
note: Recorded (Capriccio, 7:22) as 'Op. 1 No. 12, Pastorale', but Op. 1 (Naples 1697) has only 10 sonatas per IMSLP, Wikipedia and Bodleian: numbering unconfirmed

title: Trio Sonata in B-flat major, Wq. 159, H. 587
note: Work, 1755, scoring and VDE-Gallo recording (18:41, with cello and harpsichord) hold. The 'BWV Anh. 187' aka and note rest on an IMSLP 'see also'; a search summary of Bach Digital tied Anh. 187 to the F-major trio H. 588/589. Unconfirmed

title: Sonata a tre in D minor, Livre III No. 2
note: Scoring unresolved: IMSLP tags it 2 cellos + continuo (Grove: cello duet) and says the print names no instrument for the treble-clef top line. Both recordings (Cocset/Les Basses Réunies 8:39; TIEFSAITS 'A TRE', 3 cellos, 7:59) play it on cellos; 'violin or pardessus de viole' is an inference. Exists and is recorded; consider cello 2 + continuo, or drop as unspecified top instrument

title: Pavans and Galliards a 5
note: IMSLP holds two pavan-galliard pairs (VdGS 1-4), but the only viol/string recording found is one pair (Parley of Instruments, Hyperion 2024: 1:24 + 0:56; the other disc is cornetts and sackbuts). Consider one entry per pair, minutes about 3

title: Concertino for Oboe, Clarinet and String Quartet, Op. 32b
note: Floor: only recording found (Naxos 8.559253, 9:28, Ambache Chamber Orchestra and Ensemble) is billed 'oboe, clarinet and strings', not clearly the quartet version; no quartet performance found. Year: IMSLP's 1944 is the publication; Wikipedia and MusicWeb give 1939, rev. 1943 (1939-43)

title: Sonata sopra la Monica
note: IMSLP gives bassoon + continuo, or bassoon + violin (ad lib.) + continuo; the UE (Waterhouse) edition has no violin, while Seiffert (1924), TrevCo and the Brilliant recording (van Sambeek, 5:53, 'for Bassoon, Violin and Basso Continuo') use the violin. If the violin is ad lib. the work is a duo with continuo and out of scope; the owner should decide whether to count it. Year 1651, ~6 min, floor (Brilliant 2012) hold

title: Balet de village, Op. 52 No. 2
note: Work and key facts fine (Niquet 'Deuxième Ballet' 8:56). Only recording of No. 2 found is Niquet's Le Concert Spirituel (Naxos 8.554295), a directed band with several players per part; Nos. 1 and 4 have one-to-a-part recordings (Il Cuore Barocco, Umbra Lucis) but none found for No. 2. Brief requires a one-to-a-part recording. Print names musettes/vielles first

title: Balet de village, Op. 52 No. 3
note: Only recording of No. 3 found is Niquet's Le Concert Spirituel (Naxos 8.554295, 7:45), a directed band; no one-to-a-part recording found (Nos. 1 and 4 have them). Brief requires one

title: Flute Quintet in D major, Op. 21 ("Christmas Quintet")
note: Work and facts hold (D major, 1903 Doblinger, 22 min) but the floor is thin: MusicBrainz lists only the first movement (7:35) on a 1995 BBC Music Magazine cover disc; the genuin disc (Quintessenz) is an all-flute arrangement; Silvertrust names no recording

title: Trio Sonata in E minor
note: IMSLP page exists (Uppsala ms, 'Sonata da camera due violini obbligati e violoncello', no movement list). The Accent disc lists an unattributed 'Trio Sonata in E minor' (Affettuoso, Allegro, Adagio, Giga; 12:30); I could not open a source naming Brescianello as its composer. 'Dresden' in notes is unsupported (IMSLP source is Uppsala)

title: String Sextet in C major, Op. 1 No. 4
note: Floor not shown for the string version. The only recording found (Quantz Collegium, K&K 2020, live) is of the flute arrangement: Naxos record of Op. 1 No. 5 reads 'for flute, 2 violins, viola & 2 cellos... arranged for flute and string quintet'; the same group's No. 2 is titled 'Version for Flute...'. IMSLP scoring (3 vn, va, 2 vc) is right; looks like L. 270 (No. 4). No edition or string-version performance found

title: String Sextet in G major, Op. 1 No. 5
note: Floor not shown for the string version: the Quantz Collegium recording of Op. 1 No. 5 (G major, L. 271 in Naxos's uniform title) is catalogued as 'for flute, 2 violins, viola & 2 cellos', arranged for flute and string quintet. Scoring on IMSLP (3 vn, va, 2 vc) and 13 min otherwise hold. No other recording or edition found

title: Trio Sonata in A major
note: IMSLP's flute-violin-continuo sonata is from the Blancheton source, which names 'Sig. Bufardini'. The Ricercar disc has flute-continuo sonatas, and its Sonate V in A is 'arr by Le Petit Trianon' (MusicWeb): not shown to be this piece. No recording found

title: Concerto for Piano and String Quartet in D minor, Op. 17, BV 80
note: Work exists (1878, Breitkopf 1987). Only recording found (Grante, I Pomeriggi Musicali cond. Zuccarini, Music & Arts 1999) is with a conducted string ensemble; no one-to-a-part performance found

title: Trio for Harp, Violin and Viola, Op. 9 No. 1
note: Harp & Co CD titles them 'Trio for harp, violin and viola, Op. 9' (Apple and Deezer, 17:23 and 17:29, two movements each, matches the entry). But no catalogue confirms Op. 9: fr/de Wikipedia list only '2 Trios (1790)' with no opus, and the same CD's sonatas are Op. 10 where Wikipedia has Op. 11; a bookseller lists Cardon's oeuvre 9 as harp sonatas. Recorded, so they stay; the opus number and the set name rest on one CD booklet (title could become 'Trio for Harp, Violin and Viola No. 1', year 1790?).

title: Sonata in D major, Op. 9 No. 6
note: KEY CONFLICT: recording titles No. 6 'in D major' (Allegro, Largo, Rondo poco allegro); IMSLP lists the sixth key as C. Could not see the print; the title key may be wrong

title: Fantasia a 4, RC 20
note: Work exists (RC 20 = VdGS 4 = Meyer 4, 4 viols Tr T T B, Folop/WIMA edition on IMSLP) but no recording of it identified. The cited NY Consort album's 'Fantasy for Four Viols - No. 4' is programme section 'No. 4, Life', not Coprario's fantasia; MusicBrainz's 47 Coprario recordings hold no 4-part fantasia. Keep only if a recording or concert is found.

title: Flute Trio in D major
note: Year and numbering conflict. Entry year 1782-83 comes from a MusicWeb review of the Ricercar disc; IMSLP, BnF and RISM show prints by Gaveaux (1797, 'Trois trios ... 1ere suite') and Imbault ([1800], six trios), with no earlier print found. 'Op. 66' appears on the Ricercar track list and the Billaudot edition (BnF uniform title '3 trios ... Op. 66'), but Op. 66 is also Devienne's flute quartets (IMSLP, Accent recording; catalogue ids 102803-102806), and in the Billaudot first suite No. 1 is G major, not D major. Recording fine: Le Petit Trianon, Ricercar RIC416 (2020). Recorded 15:05; minutes ok. Aka 'Op. 66 No. 1' for D major is the weakest (IMSLP numbers it No. 4).

title: Lame II
note: The work is real and recorded (8 cellos, Etcetera 2002 11:10 as 'lame II'; zeitklang 2015 11:29 as 'Lame III'; Wikipedia: Lame II for 8 cellos, 1996). Only the numbering is open: IRCAM lists Lame (1982) as two solo-cello pieces, which zeitklang calls Lame I and II. Two sources for II, one for III; aka holds both

title: Suite en trio No. 4 in D major, Op. 1
note: Key 'D major' comes only from the Naxos disc, whose keys are a tone above BnF for Nos. 3 and 5; the printed key could not be found (BnF records for Nos. 1, 4, 6 not located). Consider dropping the key. Movements and 11:17 hold

title: Suite en trio No. 6 in E minor, Op. 1
note: Key 'E minor' comes only from the Naxos disc, whose keys are a tone above BnF for Nos. 3 and 5; printed key not found (it may be D minor). Consider dropping the key. Movements and 11:42 hold

title: Fantaisies à 3 parties
note: The 'set' is an editor's grouping (Yates, IMSLP 2023): in the 1610 print the three-part fantasias are scattered among the 42 (Nos. 6, 26, 29, 30 are à 3 on recordings). Recordings cover single pieces only (Savall: Nos. 6 and 26; Chelys: Nos. 29, 30), none the seven. Real music, but not a published set; consider individual fantasias or dropping

title: Notturno concertant in E-flat major, Op. 68, C. 233
note: IMSLP gives the title as 'pour fortepiano et violon (avec un cor ad libitum)': under the ad lib. rule the horn goes in optional, leaving 2 players (a duo, out of scope), though it is recorded with horn (Alpha 2018). Owner to rule

title: Testimony
note: Work and facts hold (1979-80, five statements, tracks total 23 min, premiere Krasni Quartet 1999 per IMSLP). The only recording is an album on One Media iP (probably own release) and the score is self-uploaded: composer's professional track record not shown

title: Harpsichord Concerto in C minor, Op. 14 No. 2
note: Floor: only a 2025 BMC concert (Leclair Consort, one to a part) and the 1785 Paris print on IMSLP; no recording or modern edition found. Also, a 1785 print would be piano with harpsichord alternative under the keyboard rule

title: Divertimento in E-flat major, Op. 15 No. 4 ("La partie de chasse")
note: Floor: only the 2025 BMC concert and the 1786 prints; no recording or modern edition found. If kept: IMSLP tags both harpsichord and piano, so by the keyboard rule it is piano 1, alternatives piano:[harpsichord], violin:[flute], formation piano-strings
